While the paper compares MetaMath to open-source models and GPT-3.5-Turbo, the absence of a comparison with GPT-4 leaves a gap in understanding the relative performance of MetaMath. This is crucial for assessing the true capabilities of the model and its position in the broader landscape of LLMs. Second, what is the impact of the size of the augmented dataset on the performance of MetaMath? Is there a point of diminishing returns where adding more data does not lead to significant improvements? Understanding this relationship is essential for optimizing the data augmentation process and determining the most efficient way to leverage the proposed techniques. Third, what is the performance of MetaMath on MMLU, particularly in the college-level subjects? This would provide a more comprehensive evaluation of the model's generalizability and its ability to handle different types of mathematical problems. Fourth, what is the performance of MetaMath compared with distillation from GPT-4? This would help to understand the relative effectiveness of the proposed data augmentation approach compared to other methods for improving LLM performance. Fifth, what are the specific types of errors that MetaMath makes, and are there any patterns in these errors? A detailed error analysis would provide valuable insights into the model's limitations and guide future research efforts to address these weaknesses. Finally, how does the performance of MetaMath vary across different types of mathematical problems, such as word problems, equation solving, and proof problems? This would provide a more granular understanding of the model's strengths and weaknesses and help to identify areas where further improvement is needed. These questions, which I have derived directly from my analysis of the paper, target core methodological choices and seek clarification of critical assumptions. Addressing these questions would significantly enhance the paper's contribution and provide a more complete understanding of the proposed method.
